name: Second Iconoclasm (Leo V)
summary: Emperor Leo V the Armenian summons a synod at the Hagia Sophia that reverses the decisions of the Seventh Ecumenical Council (787) and reinstates iconoclasm. The patriarch Nikephoros is deposed; Theodore the Studite leads the iconodule resistance.

_quarry.structural_significance: Second iconoclast period (815–843) renews internal Byzantine religious conflict; the resistance of figures like Theodore the Studite shapes the long-term tradition of monastic opposition to imperial doctrinal innovation.
